tips.title: Removing Old Paint from Kits
tips.text: To strip old paint from kits, use a suitable paint stripper like Citadel's 'Dettol' or 'Warm Water' paint strippers. Apply liberally, let it sit for 30 minutes, then scrub with a soft brush. Rinse thoroughly with warm water. For stubborn paint, repeat or use a stronger stripper like AK Interactive's 'Thinner Medium'. Avoid using aggressive strippers on fragile parts.

tips.title: Fixing Broken Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: Broken photo-etched parts can be repaired with CA (Cyanoacrylate) glue. Apply a small amount to the break, immediately press the parts together, and hold for a few seconds. For larger gaps, use a CA glue with accelerator like Mr. Hobby's 'Super Clear'. Avoid using too much glue, which can cause excess build-up.

tips.title: Recovering Clogged Airbrushes
tips.text: To unclog an airbrush, first disassemble and clean it thoroughly with Vallejo Airbrush Cleaner. For stubborn clogs, use a pipe cleaner dipped in acetone or a toothpick soaked in cleaner. For severe clogs, soak the airbrush overnight in acetone, then reassemble and test-spray with water until clear. Regular maintenance with Vallejo Airbrush Thinner between colors prevents clogging.

tips.title: Repairing Warped Parts
tips.text: To fix warped parts, gently bend them back into shape over a flat surface. For severe warping, soak the part in warm water for 10 minutes, then carefully bend it back. Hold in place until dry. For plastic parts, use Tamiya's 'Extra Thin Cement' along the warp, then gently bend back. Allow to set, then trim excess cement.

tips.title: Avoiding Frost from Rattle Cans
tips.text: To prevent frost from forming on painted parts when using rattle cans, apply paint in well-ventilated areas, keep parts away from direct sunlight or heat sources, and maintain a consistent temperature. Avoid painting in cold, damp environments. If frost appears, wipe immediately with a damp cloth, then allow to dry and apply a light sanding with fine-grit sandpaper before recoating.
